source: Karpathy Loop / Andrej Karpathy Autonomous Agent Architecture
summary: Karpathy published a 9-rule autonomous agent architecture document that shifts execution and bookkeeping to AI models via loop-plan-generate-review-commit cycles with disk-based state. The pattern was demonstrated running 700 experiments over 2 days autonomously.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — AgentForge already implements the loop/state-machine pattern this describes. The disk-state bookkeeping idea (artifacts) is already central to the architecture. No new gap opened.

source: Lilian Weng — Harness Engineering for AI Self-Improvement (July 2026 post)
summary: Weng's new post reframes recursive self-improvement around the harness (scaffolding, evaluation, feedback loops), not direct weight modification. Identifies harness engineering as the key bottleneck for RSI systems.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — AgentForge is itself a harness. The post validates the architecture direction but doesn't surface a specific gap not already tracked (HID-188 covers cross-run memory; HID-186 covers partial retry).

source: SYNAPSE: Episodic-Semantic Memory via Spreading Activation (arXiv 2026)
summary: SYNAPSE and related papers (MementoGUI, Membox) combine episodic memory (past run records) with semantic retrieval using spreading activation — fused BM25 + vector similarity + entity matching, yielding +29.6 points on temporal queries.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — HID-188 tracks cross-run episodic memory injection; this confirms the approach and suggests the retrieval mechanism worth incorporating. But HID-188 is already open so no new issue should be created.

source: ouro-loop — Structured Autonomous Loop for Coding Agents
summary: ouro-loop gives AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Aider, Codex) a structured autonomous loop with 5 verification gates, 3-layer self-reflection, and autonomous remediation guardrails.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — AgentForge's state machine already captures the gate/remediation pattern. The 3-layer self-reflection concept is adjacent to HID-93 (adversarial plan critique) which is already tracked.

source: LangGraph Q2 2026 releases — TimeoutPolicy, DeltaChannel, v2 streaming
summary: LangGraph added per-node TimeoutPolicy (recovery routing), node-level error handlers with Saga compensation patterns, DeltaChannel for reduced checkpoint overhead, and a v2 typed streaming API in Q2 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — Per-node timeouts and error-handler routing are analogous to what HID-167 (automatic retry with failure classification) and HID-186 (partial retry) aim to address. Both are already open issues. DeltaChannel is irrelevant (AgentForge does not use LangGraph).

source: Skill-SD: Skill-Conditioned Self-Distillation for Multi-turn LLM Agents (arXiv 2604.10674)
summary: Introduces skill-conditioned self-distillation where agents learn reusable behavioral skills from successful trajectories, then condition future runs on those skills to improve multi-turn success rates.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — AgentForge already shipped skill distillation (distillationAgent.ts, agentSkillRepository.ts). The paper validates the approach. Known remaining gap (executor not receiving skills) is tracked under HID-188. No net-new gap.

summary: ByteDance's DeerFlow v2.0 hit #1 GitHub Trending in Feb 2026. Implements long-horizon task decomposition with sub-agent delegation, multi-step planning, and structured intermediate artifact passing between stages.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses Linear issues as the task unit rather than decomposing within a single run. Sub-agent delegation would require parallel execution (deliberately deferred). The artifact-passing pattern already exists.

source: Recursive Self-Evolving Agents via Held-Out Selection (arXiv 2606.28374)
summary: Proposes held-out validation sets for selecting which agent self-modifications to keep, as a guard against degenerate self-improvement. Addresses the evaluation-loop problem in recursive self-improvement.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — Requires RL-style training infrastructure. AgentForge is a deterministic orchestrator, not a self-modifying agent. Pattern is too speculative for near-term adoption.
